judged_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:122-124,147-149 — the organizer-email override uses the first array element (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`) while the actual `calendarId` used to insert the event is chosen by matching `cal.credentialId === credentialId`; for multi-host collective events these two selection strategies diverge, so the attendee/organizer entry can carry a different host's calendar email than the calendar the event is actually written to (P2, confidence 75).

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the organizer attendee email is overridden using the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...;` then `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : organizer.email`), while the target `calendarId` for `events.insert` is chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. With multi-destination arrays (introduced by this diff, e.g. collective/team events), these can point to different calendars/hosts, so the event can be inserted into one calendar while the organizer attendee/email reflects a different destination calendar. Same pattern exists in `updateEvent`.
